meaning:
ψεύδω to deceive by lies; more frequently in the depon. mid, form ψεύδομαι (so always in NT),
[in LXX chiefly for כָּחַשׁ pi. ;]
1. absol., to lie: Heb.6:18, 1Jn.1:6, Rev.3:9; οὐ ψεύδομαι, Rom.9:1, 2Co.11:31, Gal.1:20, 1Ti.2:7 with dative of person(s) (Psa.18:45, Jhn.5:12, al.), Act.5:4; before εἰς, Col.3:9; κατά, Jas.3:14 (Hort, in l).
2. Like act., with accusative, to deceive by lies (Æsch., al.): Act.5:3.†
(AS)

I tell the truth in Christ. I am not lying, my conscience testifying with me in the Holy Spirit
The God and Father of the Lord Jesus Christ, he who is blessed forever more, knows that I don’t lie.
Now about the things which I write to you, behold, before God, I’m not lying.
Don’t lie to one another, seeing that you have put off the old man with his doings,
to which I was appointed a preacher and an apostle—I am telling the truth in Christ, not lying—a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
that by two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have a strong encouragement, who have fled for refuge to take hold of the hope…
